facts.detail: Ofcom published the vulnerable-people page on 30 November 2022.
Vulnerability can be temporary or permanent.
Physical or mental health problems can create vulnerability.
Age and literacy skills are examples of relevant characteristics.
Bereavement, job loss and household-income changes can create vulnerability.
Ofcom wants vulnerable people to receive good customer care.
Ofcom expects access to appropriate help, support and services.
The work aims to protect vulnerable customers and help them engage in communications markets.
Customers should be able to make informed choices and be treated fairly.
The fairness programme covers home phone, broadband, mobile and pay-TV services.

guard_streams.source: Treating vulnerable customers fairly: a guide for phone, broadband and pay-TV providers
guard_streams.write_limit: Provider good-practice guidance for vulnerable customers is not selected-parcel broadband evidence.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the consultation on 25 September 2019.
The consultation closed on 20 November 2019.
The page status is Statement Published and closed.
The guide was last updated on 29 September 2022.
It suggests measures providers can adopt to treat vulnerable people fairly.
The guide promotes a high level of customer care.
It aims to help vulnerable customers obtain an appropriate deal at a fair price.
General Conditions C5.1 to C5.5 require relevant policies and procedures.
The page cites 37% of people with mental-health experience showing significant anxiety with essential-service providers.
The 2022 update added measures on debt, payment difficulty, free debt advice and social tariffs.

guard_streams.source: Telecoms price rises – what are your rights?
guard_streams.write_limit: Contract-price rules and savings advice do not establish selected-parcel broadband coverage or measured performance.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the price-rise guide on 20 January 2023.
The guide was last updated on 29 June 2026.
In-contract price rises often occur once a year in March or April.
Inflation-linked price rises are banned for new contracts.
Since January 2025, new contracts cannot express rises as inflation links or percentages.
Specified rises must be stated clearly in pounds and pence before sign-up.
Price-rise information must be prominent and transparent.
Providers must state when monthly-price changes will occur.
Contracts signed before 17 January 2025 may retain percentage or inflation-linked terms.
Unexpected or excessive rises require at least 30 days' notice and a 30-day exit window.

guard_streams.write_limit: Affordability research and social-tariff monitoring do not prove physical network serviceability or measured parcel speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the affordability page on 12 December 2023.
The page was last updated on 4 February 2026.
Affordable fixed broadband is an Ofcom priority.
Affordable mobile internet is also an Ofcom priority.
The stated aim is access to high-quality services at affordable prices.
Ofcom has published affordability reports since December 2020.
The reports summarise communications-affordability research.
The work tracks availability, awareness and take-up of broadband social tariffs.
Social tariffs are cheaper packages for people receiving Universal Credit or other benefits.
Ofcom reports that social-tariff take-up among eligible households remains low.

guard_streams.source: Pricing and consumer engagement 2025: interactive report
guard_streams.write_limit: Aggregate pricing, switching, affordability and debt analysis does not verify broadband availability or speed at a selected parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the 2025 interactive report on 26 February 2026.
The report covers UK residential fixed-broadband prices.
It covers residential fixed-voice services.
It covers residential mobile-phone services.
It covers pay TV and subscription video-on-demand services.
The analysis includes tariffs offered in bundles.
It also includes standalone tariffs.
The report examines how much customers pay.
It examines consumer engagement and switching.
The scope includes affordability and customer debt.
